title: Find Google spreadsheets with AI by name or content
h1: find the google spreadsheet before opening its rows
description: Use a bot to find Google spreadsheets by filename, content, dates or sharing status. Understand prefix matches and incomplete shared-drive searches.
keyword: google sheets search spreadsheets with ai
answer: **the supplier sent the sheet. now the link is buried.** a bot finds accessible google spreadsheets by name, content, dates or sharing status. it returns candidate files without changing cells. name searches start at the beginning of filenames, so give it the opening words or ask for a broader match when you only remember the middle.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: find the spreadsheet before the cell work.
what:
**start with the bit of the filename you remember.** name mode matches from the beginning. you can also find starred files, shared files or spreadsheets changed after a date.

content search covers names and descriptions too. ask where the word matched before assuming it came from a cell. have the bot gather the full result list. already have the link? use it and skip the hunt.
uses: **recover supplier prices.** find a shared sheet after losing the email with its link.
**resume planning.** collect starred spreadsheets changed since the project restarted.
**find a project’s trackers.** search filenames beginning with its project code.
**search beyond the title.** use a venue clue when you forget the spreadsheet name.

routine.message:
every other thursday at 09:50, find google spreadsheets shared with me whose names begin "brackenport supplier".

- include shared drives
- finish reading all results
- return candidate names and file references here
- say if the shared-drive search is incomplete

never edit cells or export files. if names are ambiguous, leave the choice to me.
routine.needs: google sheets connected with read only; allow only spreadsheet search
routine.output:
brackenport supplier candidates
- brackenport supplier rates - west
- brackenport supplier contacts
2 file references ready to open.

steps: **keep the lookup read only.** connect google sheets for this bot.
**allow search only.** limit its app actions to spreadsheet search.
**try the name’s beginning.** if that misses, try a content clue.
**open the closest candidate.** once it finds the right files, schedule the search and update the prefix as the project changes.
watch: **a content match can come from the title.** read the cells separately before claiming a row contains your term.
**name a shared drive when a familiar file is missing.** searches across shared drives can be incomplete; an empty list is not a full inventory.
**trash stays out by default.** ask to include it when recovering a discarded tracker.

faq.q: why does a word in the middle of the filename miss?
faq.a: **name mode starts at the beginning.** ask the bot to search anywhere in the filename instead.

faq.q: does this read every row too?
faq.a: **no, it finds spreadsheet files.** choose one, then ask to read the relevant cells with a separate action.

steps: connect google sheets with read only
ask for filenames beginning with a familiar project name
request all candidates and any search gaps
choose the file before asking about its cells

mistakes.mistake: assuming content means cell contents only
mistakes.fix: ask where the word matched. a title or description can cause the result.

mistakes.mistake: searching again when you already have the link
mistakes.fix: give the bot the link and move on to the range you need.

tip.text: if you remember only the middle of the name, say that. a prefix search will miss it.
